title: Clean Schedule
description: A dispatcher builds out a full day of back-to-back, non-overlapping assignments across a small fleet. Prove the conflict detector stays quiet when it should — a naive overlap check that's off by one boundary condition would wrongly flag adjacent, non-overlapping slots.
successCondition: Book three shipments. Assign all three to the same vehicleId and same driverId with strictly back-to-back windows (e.g. 08:00-10:00, 10:00-12:00, 12:00-14:00 — each scheduledEnd exactly equal to the next scheduledStart). All three PUT calls succeed. GET /api/fleet/conflicts returns conflicts with no entry referencing any of these three assignment ids — touching boundaries are correctly treated as non-overlapping.
hints: The overlap check is a < b.end && b.start < a.end (strict inequalities) — touching endpoints (a.end === b.start) should NOT count as overlapping, which is exactly what this test pins down.
Double-check your three time windows really do touch exactly at the boundary with no gap and no overlap — a one-second mismatch either way changes what you're proving.
